body.statement:
There are numerical constants \(c,C<\infty\) and events \(\mathcal E_n\) such that
\[
 \inf_{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa}P(\mathcal E_n)
 \geq 1-Cn^{-3}.
\]
If \(n_1\geq1\), then, on \(\mathcal E_n\), simultaneously for every
\(h\in H_n\) and \(u\in U_n\) satisfying
\(n_1u\geq C\log(en)\),
\[
 J_P(h,u)
 \leq \widehat J\!\left(h,c\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)
 \leq C\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h,C\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)\right\}.                 \tag{P1}
\]
On the same event,
\[
 a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)                              \tag{P2}
\]
for every \(x\in B\) and \(h\in H_n\), and
\[
 \tfrac12a_P(x,h)\leq a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)\leq2a_P(x,h) \tag{P3}
\]
whenever \(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\).  For every \(h\in H_n\), the
source-labeled sorting, duplicate removal, deterministic refinement, and
midpoint operations defining \(C_1(h)\) and \(G_1(h)\) are Borel functions
of \((X_i)_{i\in I_1}\), and \(\widehat J(h,v)\) is Borel for every
\(v\geq0\).  In particular, the upper comparison in \((\mathrm{P1})\) uses
the same radius \(h\), and the floor \(1\vee J_P\) covers an empty population
thin set.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(m=n_1\) and \(\ell=\log(en)\).  When \(m=0\), the condition
\(mu\geq C\ell\) has no solutions, and the definitions give
\(q_t^L=0\leq q_t\leq1=q_t^U\), hence \((\mathrm{P2})\).  We may therefore
assume \(m\geq1\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(s\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and \(h\in H_n\), define
\[
 \mathcal C_{t,s,h}
 =\{z\in A_t:\|z-(0,s)\|_2\leq h\}.
\]
For deterministic \(z_i=(r_i,s_i)\), membership of \(z_i\) in this set,
as a function of \(s\), is zero unless \(z_i\in A_t\) and \(|r_i|\leq h\);
otherwise it is the indicator of the closed interval
\[
 [s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},\,s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}].                  \tag{P4}
\]
Thus the trace on \(N\) points changes only at at most \(2N\) endpoints.
Since \(|H_n|\leq2+\log_2n\), the shatter coefficient of
\[
 \mathcal C_n=\{\mathcal C_{t,s,h}:t\in\{0,1\},
 \ s\in[-1/2,1/2],\ h\in H_n\}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal C_n}(N)
 \leq2|H_n|(2N+1)\leq C_0(N+1)\ell.                              \tag{P5}
\]

We prove the relative empirical inequality used below.  For a measurable
set class \(\mathcal A\), an empirical law \(P_m\) based on \(m\) independent
observations, and
\(\Gamma=x+\log\{8\Pi_{\mathcal A}(2m)\}\), \(x\geq1\),
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal A:
 |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{\frac{2P_m(C)\Gamma}{m}}+\frac{7\Gamma}{3m}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-x}.                                                     \tag{P6}
\]
To derive it, introduce an independent empirical law \(P'_m\), condition on
the pooled \(2m\) observations, pair them, and independently choose which
member of each pair enters \(P_m\).  For a fixed pooled trace, the difference
of its two counts is a sum of independent signs over at most
\(2m\bar p\) discordant pairs, where
\(\bar p=(P_m(C)+P'_m(C))/2\).  The identity
\(\cosh(v)\leq e^{v^2/2}\), exponential Markov, and optimization give
\[
 \Pr\{|P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|>2\sqrt{\bar pz/m}\mid\text{pooled sample}\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                                     \tag{P7}
\]
Peel \(\bar p\) into \(2^{-j-1}<\bar p\leq2^{-j}\), use
\(z=\Gamma+(j+1)\log2\), and union over at most
\(\Pi_{\mathcal A}(2m)\) traces.  The probabilities sum geometrically.
For the ghost-sample reduction, if
\(d=|P_m(C)-P(C)|\) violates \((\mathrm{P6})\), the independent ghost half
has conditional probability at least \(1/4\) of satisfying
\[
 |P_m(C)-P'_m(C)|
 >\sqrt{4\bar p\Gamma/m}+2\Gamma/(3m).
\]
This follows on substituting \(P(C)\leq P_m(C)+d\) for a downward deviation,
\(P(C)\leq P_m(C)\) for an upward deviation, and using
\(2\sqrt{d\Gamma/m}\leq d/2+2\Gamma/m\).  Multiplication by four proves
\((\mathrm{P6})\).  The argument uses only pooled traces, so increasing
finite trace subfamilies covers a nonattained supremum.

Apply \((\mathrm{P6})\) to \(\mathcal C_n\) with \(x=3\ell\).
By \((\mathrm{P5})\), \(\Gamma\leq6\ell\) for \(n\geq2\), and hence
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal C_n:
 |P_m(C)-P(C)|>
 \sqrt{12P_m(C)\ell/m}+20\ell/m\right\}
 \leq C_1n^{-3}.                                                   \tag{P8}
\]
The closed intervals in \((\mathrm{P4})\) include traces attained at all
breakpoint ties.  Let \(\mathcal E_n\) be the complement of this event.
Since \(P_m(\mathcal C_{t,s,h})=\widehat q_t^{(1)}((0,s),h)\),
\((\mathrm{P8})\) and the definitions imply
\[
 q_t^L(x,h)\leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)                           \tag{P9}
\]
simultaneously in \(x,t,h\), and taking minima proves \((\mathrm{P2})\).
If \(mq_t(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), solving the two quadratic inequalities in
\((\mathrm{P8})\) gives
\[
 \tfrac12q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^L(x,h)
 \leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)\leq2q_t(x,h).                       \tag{P10}
\]
When \(ma_P(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), this holds on both sides, and taking minima
proves \((\mathrm{P3})\).

Fix \(h\).  Every endpoint in \((\mathrm{P4})\) generated by a first-half
score and lying in the target segment occurs in the source-labeled list.
Lexicographic order is total, and retaining the least label at equal
coordinates retains the common breakpoint.  A deterministic mesh point tied
with a breakpoint likewise occurs once.  Define \(g_h((0,s))=(0,s)\) at
each listed coordinate and otherwise map \(s\) to the midpoint of its unique
open cell.  No first-half membership indicator changes in an open cell.
Because \(M_h=\lceil16/h\rceil\), consecutive deterministic mesh points are
at distance at most \(h/16\).  Therefore, including at every tie,
\[
 \|g_h(x)-x\|_2\leq h/32<h/4,\qquad
 \widehat q_t^{(1)}(g_h(x),h)=\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h).             \tag{P11}
\]

Let \(F\) be \(h\)-separated and contained in
\(\{x:a_P(x,h)\leq u\}\).  For each \(x\in F\), choose \(t_x\) with
\(q_{t_x}(x,h)\leq u\).  On \(\mathcal E_n\), putting
\(z=\widehat q_{t_x}^{(1)}(x,h)\) in \((\mathrm{P8})\) and solving gives
\(z\leq2u+64\ell/m\).  Applying the definition of \(b_n\) and
\(2\sqrt{uv}\leq u+v\), then using \((\mathrm{P11})\), yields
\[
 a^U(g_h(x),h)\leq C_3\{u+\ell/m\}.                               \tag{P12}
\]
For distinct \(x,x'\in F\),
\[
 \|g_h(x)-g_h(x')\|_2\geq h-h/32-h/32=15h/16>h/2.                \tag{P13}
\]
The upward rounding satisfies
\[
 u(v)\leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\},                                    \tag{P14}
\]
including \(v=0\), directly from adjacent dyadic ratio two and the smallest
positive grid value.  Choosing the numerical \(c\) large enough makes
\(g_h(F)\) feasible for
\(\widehat J(h,c\{u+\ell/m\})\); \((\mathrm{P13})\) makes the map injective.
Taking the maximum proves the first inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\), also
when \(u=1\).

Conversely, let \(G\) be nonempty and feasible in \(\widehat J(h,v)\).
Equations \((\mathrm{P2})\) and \((\mathrm{P14})\) give
\[
 a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\leq u(v)
 \leq\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\},\qquad g\in G.                           \tag{P15}
\]
Order \(G=\{g_1<\cdots<g_M\}\) on \(B\).  Feasibility and collinearity give
\[
 \|g_{j+2}-g_j\|_2
 =\|g_{j+2}-g_{j+1}\|_2+\|g_{j+1}-g_j\|_2\geq h.                 \tag{P16}
\]
The odd and even sublists are thus \(h\)-separated at the same physical
radius \(h\), and \((\mathrm{P15})\) makes both feasible for the population
packing.  Hence
\[
 |G|\leq2J_P(h,\min\{1,2v+m^{-1}\}).                             \tag{P17}
\]
If the finite maximum is empty, the outer floor is one.  Substitute
\(v=c\{u+\ell/m\}\), enlarge \(C\), and combine the two cases to prove the
upper inequality in \((\mathrm{P1})\) with \(1\vee J_P\).  No radius
monotonicity has been used.

Finally, the square-root endpoint map is continuous on its closed domain.
Candidate inclusion, lexicographic comparisons, finite sorting, least-label
tie removal, deterministic refinement, and midpoint formation are Borel.
The finite maximum defining \(\widehat J\) is a maximum of finitely many
Borel feasibility indicators after absent slots are encoded by their Borel
presence indicators.  This proves all measurability assertions and completes
the proof.
body.justification: The lemma remains a pure first-half, tie-safe same-radius comparison with the mandatory unit floor.
body.gap: It does not itself make an outcome-risk assertion; that role is now discharged by the separate severity-net extension lemma.
body.consumer: The anchor construction uses its confidence bounds, pattern representative, and exact-radius population comparison.
